premise_accepted_quote: As described, the evidence shows the marker is **prognostic**: marker-positive patients do worse regardless of treatment. That's useful, but it doesn't establish that the marker is **predictive**
factual_errors_vs_key: Says a mechanistic link plus a single preclinical figure of differential response is enough to call it a predictive rationale, whereas the key requires treatment-by-marker interaction evidence (ideally randomised) or a mechanistic link plus dose/exposure response in marker-positive subjects

Does not warn that enriching on a purely prognostic marker can make the trial harder to read, and does not mention post hoc subgroup prespecification or multiplicity control (only partially mentions prespecified assay cutoff)
States marker-positive patients do worse 'regardless of treatment', which overstates what untreated/mixed-treatment cohorts show
